newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat ends Jordan talks with King Hussein.
newsitem.headline: Arafat ends Jordan talks with King Hussein.

text.p: Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat discussed in Amman on Tuesday latest Middle East developments with King Hussein of Jordan, who underwent minor knee surgery three days ago, officials said.

The state news agency Petra said Arafat congratulated the king on his recuperation from the minor operation and "discussed the latest developments on the peace process and especially the Palestinian-Israeli track after the Hebron accord."
Officials said Arafat had earlier reviewed bilateral ties with Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti in expanded talks between the delegations.
They said agreement was reached to hold a meeting in the next month of the Jordanian-Palestinian committee that oversees ties between the two sides and to activate a number of bilateral accords.
Arafat had been due to visit on Monday but officials said bad weather forced a postponement.
King Hussein had minor surgery on Saturday on both his knees. One was to remove a cartilage and another to repair damage caused during his pilgrimage to Mecca last Thursday.

Tuesday's meeting is the first between Arafat and King Hussein since the Jordanian monarch flew to Gaza and Tel Aviv two weeks ago to help break a deadlock in Palestinian-Israeli talks on the West Bank town of Hebron.
The two sides finally agreed after months of delay on details of an Israeli troop withdrawal from 80 percent of Hebron and a timetable for further redeployment from the West Bank.
